_comment: invent.c sortloot() and sortloot_cmp(): loot_classify() runs lazily inside the comparator and, when the hero can see, marks each object encountered (o_init.c observe_object()), so the order of discoveries within a class follows the order in which the C library's qsort() first compares the objects (nethack-c/patches/002-deterministic-qsort.patch). macOS and glibc call the comparator in different orders, so record this recipe on macOS (.github/workflows/macos-recorder.yml), not with a Linux recorder; see docs/testing.md, "The qsort() call order". A blindfolded Priest wishes for five rings, drops them and then a clove of garlic on one square, takes the blindfold off, opens the pick-up menu (pickup.c query_objlist(), six objects) and reads his discoveries.
